title: Surgical Table: Assemble Your First Bionic Creature
placing.title: Placing Donors
placing.intro: Surgical Tables let you dissect mimics and assemble parts from different donors into a new creature
placing.surface: Adjacent Surgical Tables connect to form one continuous work surface
placing.cultivate: First grow a mimic in a Slime Petri Dish. See its Ponder scenes to learn more
placing.capture: Use a Capture Net or Cardboard Box to capture a mimic, then right-click the table to place it
placing.irreversible: Placing a mimic on the table turns it into surgical parts. This conversion is irreversible
placing.multiple: Multiple mimics can share the same work surface
placing.redstone: Power any part of the connected work surface to display the creatures' original appearance
recombining.title: Cutting and Reassembling
recombining.tools: Use tools to dissect and reassemble creatures on the table
recombining.cut: Right-click a connection with Shears to separate the model into individual cubes
recombining.move: Use a Cardboard Box to pick up and reposition an entire connected component
recombining.replace: Take the parts you need from other donors, then select two attachment points with Super Glue to replace the original body structure
recombining.kit: Surgical Tables support many other tools. Craft a Surgical Kit to switch between them quickly
recombining.more_tools: The functions of more tools will be introduced in later chapters.
joints.title: Installing Joints
joints.hopping: Without joints, the assembled creature can only hop and deal contact damage like a slime
joints.intro: You need to install joints to give it the ability to turn its head, swing its arms and walk
joints.types_upper: Neck Joints correspond to the head; Shoulder and Elbow Joints to the upper arms and forearms; Hip and Knee Joints to the upper and lower legs
joints.order: First right-click the moving cube, such as an upper arm, then its supporting cube, such as the torso
joints.contact: Joints can only be installed between two directly connected cubes
joints.stats_intro: The finished mimic's base attributes change with factors such as the volume of the corresponding body parts
joints.stats_shape: For example, greater overall volume means more health; greater arm volume means more damage; longer legs mean faster movement
traits.title: Introducing Traits
traits.intro: Besides changing the creature's appearance and base stats, retained donor tissue can give it unique bionic traits
traits.example: For example, combine a Creeper's Self-Destruct with a Phantom's Winged Flight...
traits.result: and you get a living bomber
traits.donors: Mix tissue from different creatures to combine the traits they provide
traits.scope: Each trait has its own scope. Some affect the whole body, while others work only in the relevant body part
traits.joints: Joints determine which body part the tissue belongs to
traits.rules: Some traits only require the relevant tissue (presence). Others require a minimum share (threshold) or vary in effect with the tissue share (scaled)
traits.volume: The tissue share is measured within the trait's scope. Self-Destruct is a torso trait, so Phantom tissue mounted on the arms does not affect it
traits.mind: Disposition and Intelligence are the most basic traits. They affect target selection and combat strategy, respectively
traits.inspect: Hold a Cardboard Box and hover over a creature on the Surgical Table to see its traits and missing requirements. Gray entries are inactive
traits.adjust: Use the hints to adjust the tissue, its placement and the joints. Check the result again to work toward the traits you want
traits.jei: Look up the Surgical Table's recipes in JEI to see each trait's effect, requirements and donors
traits.lookup: You can also look up traits from donor previews, spawn eggs or filled Cardboard Boxes
